summary: This note describes the 1974 NBA draft, the 28th annual NBA draft, held May 28, 1974, before the 1974–75 season. It covers the draft order (set by a coin flip for the first two picks, then reverse win–loss order), franchise changes such as the Capital Bullets becoming the Washington Bullets and the New Orleans Jazz's debut, and eligibility rules including the 'hardship' rule. The draft had 10 rounds and 178 selections.
one_line: Overview of the 28th NBA draft, held May 28, 1974, covering draft order, eligibility rules and the 178-player, 10-round selection.
key_facts: The 1974 NBA draft was the 28th annual draft of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
The draft was held on May 28, 1974, before the 1974–75 season.
18 NBA teams took turns selecting amateur U.S. college basketball players and other eligible players, including international players.
The first two picks belonged to the teams that finished last in each conference, with the order determined by a coin flip.
The Portland Trail Blazers won the coin flip and were awarded the first overall pick.
The Philadelphia 76ers were awarded the second overall pick.
The remaining first-round picks and subsequent rounds were assigned in reverse order of win–loss record in the previous season.
Prior to the draft, the Capital Bullets were renamed the Washington Bullets.
The expansion New Orleans Jazz took part in the NBA Draft for the first time and were assigned the tenth pick in each round.
A player who had finished his four-year college eligibility was eligible for selection.
If a player left college early, he would not be eligible for selection until his college class graduated.
Before the draft, 20 college underclassmen were declared eligible under the "hardship" rule after showing evidence of financial hardship to the league.
The draft consisted of 10 rounds comprising the selection of 178 players.
